papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Outcomes following curative-intent resection of synchronous primary lung cancer (SPLC) remain incompletely defined. We compared recurrence and survival in SPLC versus solitary primary tumors among patients with clinical stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of Veterans undergoing curative-intent resection for clinical stage I NSCLC in the Veterans Health Administration (2006-2020). SPLC was defined as two distinct clinical stage I NSCLC tumors diagnosed within six weeks, with curative-intent treatment of both tumors within one year. Propensity score matching (PSM) (1:1) was used to compare patients with SPLC to those with solitary tumors. The primary outcome was cumulative incidence of recurrence (CIR); secondary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). Additional analyses examined the role of adjuvant treatment and drivers of recurrence in SPLC patients. RESULTS: Of 12,606 Veterans with resected clinical stage I NSCLC, 337 (2.7%) had SPLC. SPLC presented with larger tumors and more advanced pathologic stage. Histology was discordant between the two tumors in 44.2% of SPLC cases. In the propensity-matched cohort (281 pairs), SPLC was associated with higher CIR (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.10-2.07), worse DFS (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.03-1.50), and worse OS (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.01-1.45). Within SPLC, wedge resection of both tumors was independently associated with recurrence. CONCLUSIONS: After adjustment, SPLC was associated with higher recurrence and worse survival than solitary tumors, supporting recognition of SPLC as a higher-risk phenotype within clinical stage I NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Consolidation immunotherapy improves outcomes after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Disease progression remains common, and more effective consolidation strategies are needed. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of benmelstobart with or without anlotinib as consolidation therapy after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter double-blind phase 3 randomized clinical trial took place at 42 centers in China from 2020 to 2023 among patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after concurrent or sequential chemoradiotherapy. In stage 1, patients were randomized 1:1:1 to 2 active regimens or placebo; in stage 2, additional patients were randomized 1:1 between the active regimens to power their direct comparison. Data cutoffs were November 30, 2023, for stage 1 and July 8, 2024, for the pooled analysis. Data analysis was performed from January 17 to March 23, 2025. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to receive benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart plus anlotinib placebo, or their matching placebos. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary end point was independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS). RESULTS: Of 553 participants (median [IQR] age, 62 [56-67] years; 495 male individuals [89.5%]), 390 were randomized in stage 1 and 163 in stage 2. In stage 1, median PFS was 15.1 months (95% CI, 9.4-21.7) with benmelstobart plus anlotinib, 9.7 months (95% CI, 6.0-34.4) with benmelstobart alone, and 4.2 months (95% CI, 3.2-6.8) with placebo. The hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.49 (95% CI, 0.36-0.66; P < .001) for benmelstobart plus anlotinib vs placebo and 0.53 (95% CI, 0.39-0.72; P < .001) for benmelstobart vs placebo. In the pooled stage 1 and 2 analysis, median PFS was 17.4 (95% CI, 12.5-24.8) months with benmelstobart plus anlotinib and 11.2 (95% CI, 7.0-20.7) months with benmelstobart alone (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.63-1.08; P = .12). Grade 3 to 5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 48.8%, 29.4%, and 19.7% in the benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart alone, and placebo groups, respectively; grade 5 events occurred in 7.2%, 1.4%, and 1.5%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that benmelstobart with or without anlotinib significantly improved PFS compared with placebo. Adding anlotinib did not significantly improve PFS compared with benmelstobart alone and increased severe and fatal treatment-related adverse events. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04325763.

papers.abstract_en: We examined whether the impact on quality of life (QOL) of early palliative care delivered via video versus in-person visits varied across patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Between 6/2018 and 5/2023, 1250 patients with advanced NSCLC enrolled in a randomized trial comparing early palliative care delivered via video or in-person visits at 22 cancer centers. Using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Lung scale, we examined whether the effect of palliative care delivery modality on patient-reported QOL at 24 weeks post-enrollment varied by baseline sociodemographic and other factors. Black patients, Hispanic/Latino patients, and those with incomes <$50,000 reported better QOL in the video visit group versus the in-person group. However, Asian patients in the video visit group reported worse QOL than the in-person group. Early palliative care delivered via video may provide greater QOL benefits for Black and Hispanic/Latino patients with advanced NSCLC and those with lower incomes. Trial Registration: NCT03375489.

papers.abstract_en: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remains one of the most lethal thoracic malignancies, characterized by rapid progression, early metastasis, and limited durable responses to conventional therapy. Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3), a Notch pathway inhibitory ligand aberrantly overexpressed on the surface of approximately 70-85% of SCLC tumor cells but largely absent from normal adult tissue, has emerged as a compelling and therapeutically actionable target. Early efforts to exploit DLL3 through the antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) rovalpituzumab tesirine (Rova-T) yielded important mechanistic insights despite failing to demonstrate survival benefit in phase III trials and have since catalyzed a new generation of more refined DLL3-directed strategies. This review critically examines the evolving portfolio of DLL3-targeted therapies across three principal modalities: T-cell engagers, ADCs, and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies. In parallel, we examine emerging non-DLL3 therapeutic strategies reshaping the broader SCLC landscape. We additionally discuss the translational science underpinning DLL3 as a biomarker, including the emerging roles of circulating tumor cell-based liquid biopsy and DLL3-directed immunoPET-CT imaging in patient selection and treatment monitoring.

papers.abstract_en: Surgical repair of gastroesophageal (GE) defects is a formidable clinical challenge, plagued by high leakage, fistula recurrence and life-threatening complications due to gastric acid exposure and persistent mechanical stress. To address this unmet need, we developed a robust bio-supportive (RBS) hydrogel patch for immediate fluid-tight closure and full-thickness tissue regeneration. Fabricated from highly crystalline polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogel, the RBS patch has a double-disc architecture, inherent porous network and weakly bound water. The double-disc design ensures effective sealing and deformation resistance; high crystallinity confers adequate mechanical strength and long-term acid/enzyme resistance. Moreover, its porous microstructure and weakly bound water synergistically promote cellular adhesion, migration and tissue infiltration for functional repair. In rat and rabbit models, the RBS patch achieved remarkable healing of gastric perforations (GP), esophageal perforations (EP) and tracheoesophageal fistulas (TEF), with intact mucosal, submucosal and muscular layers regeneration. Its efficacy and safety were further validated in beagle dog models, highlighting clinical translation potential. This RBS patch serves as a versatile bio-supportive technology for GE defects and a promising platform for tissue repair in dynamic physiological environments.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Subspecialty interstitial lung disease (ILD) clinics are associated with improved outcomes, yet access remains uneven. Even within tertiary health systems, patients with ILD are managed across diverse ambulatory settings, with unclear implications for care and outcomes. RESEARCH QUESTION: Within a single academic health system, do patient characteristics, care delivery, and outcomes differ between individuals with ILD managed in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus other ambulatory settings? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with ILD at a large academic medical center. Identified patients were stratified by care in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus non-specialty setting. Demographic, diagnostic testing, treatment, health care utilization, and survival data were extracted from the electronic health record. Diagnostic and treatment measures were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Hospitalization, emergency department visit, and death were analyzed as time-to-event outcomes. RESULTS: Among 6,637 patients with ILD, 4,371 (66%) were seen in the subspecialty ILD clinic. The 2,266 patients (34%) managed in non-specialty settings were more likely to identify as Black or Latinx, reside in more socioeconomically deprived neighborhoods, and have an unspecified ILD diagnosis (all p < 0.001). In the peri-diagnostic period, ILD clinic care was associated with higher adjusted odds of chest CT imaging (OR 2.51, 2.07-3.05) and antifibrotic therapy (OR 1.54, 1.32-1.80), and lower odds of lung biopsy (OR 0.47, 0.32-0.68). ILD clinic care was associated with a lower adjusted hazards of all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.46, 0.42-0.51), emergency department visit (HR 0.68, 0.59-0.78), and death (HR 0.57, 0.45-0.72). P-value <0.001 for all. INTERPRETATION: Within a single health system, subspecialty ILD clinic care was associated with more guideline-concordant care and improved outcomes. Differences in access to subspecialty expertise may contribute to inequities in care delivery, underscoring the need for scalable strategies, referral optimization, telemedicine, and clinical decision support, to extend ILD expertise and improve outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Azithromycin reduces exacerbations in chronic airway disease, but whether it alters the risk of nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) isolation is unresolved. RESEARCH QUESTION: Is azithromycin exposure in the preceding year associated with incident respiratory NTM isolation in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis and in COPD? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Two nationwide register-based nested case-control analyses in Denmark. Case patients had a first positive respiratory culture for NTM; controls, alive and free of prior NTM isolation on the index date, were matched 1:20 on age, sex, and comorbidity index. The prespecified exposure was at least 3,000 mg of azithromycin with at least two prescriptions redeemed in the preceding 12 months, with a 3-month lag. Conditional logistic regression was adjusted for inhaled and oral corticosteroids. Exploratory analyses examined an active comparator at matched thresholds, recency, and outcome stringency. RESULTS: The analyses comprised 173 cases and 3,409 controls (bronchiectasis) and 365 and 7,300 (COPD). papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Only a subset of patients with esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) achieve complete or partial histopathological response to immunotherapy, highlighting the need for better understanding of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Despite efforts to characterize the EAC TME at the molecular level, its epigenetic landscape remains understudied. METHODS: We combined bulk DNA methylation data from a large Norwegian multicenter EAC cohort (n = 232) with immune gene annotations to identify immune-related CpG sites differentially methylated between tumor and normal tissue. Hierarchical consensus clustering of EAC samples based on these sites was performed, and the identified subtypes were characterized according to their immune cell type composition, association with clinical features and potential prognostic relevance. RESULTS: We identified four immune subtypes (IS1-IS4) with distinct DNA methylation patterns and tumor-infiltrating immune cell composition. The highest DNA methylation levels at immune-related CpG sites were found in IS3, which showed the lowest relative fractions of CD8+ T cells and the highest fractions of regulatory T cells (Tregs), consistent with an immunosuppressed phenotype. Conversely, IS1, with the lowest DNA methylation levels at immune-related CpG sites, displayed the highest relative fractions of CD8+ T cells and the lowest fractions of Tregs, aligning with an "inflamed" immune profile. These findings were validated in an independent multicenter cohort (n = 285). No significant differences in 5-year overall survival were observed across immune subtypes, possibly reflecting the influence of variable response to neoadjuvant treatment. CONCLUSION: The identified immune subtypes offer new insights into the epigenetic landscape of the EAC TME and reveal differences in its cellular composition.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) is performed in patients with traumatic cardiac arrest or peri-arrest to treat potentially reversible causes of circulatory collapse. Optimal patient selection and timing remain uncertain, and existing evidence is largely retrospective, often excluding prehospital deaths. This prospective service evaluation examined contemporary RT practice and outcomes across a national major trauma system, including prehospital and emergency department settings. METHODS: Prospective 12-month observational study across 20 UK Helicopter Emergency Medical Services and 26 Major Trauma Centre Emergency Departments, using the PHOTON, TERN, and NaTRIC research networks. RESULTS: A total of 116 patients underwent RT, of which 82 (70.7%) were performed prehospital. Median age was 30 years, 97 patients (83.6%) were male, and 81 (69.8%) sustained penetrating injury. Suspected cardiac tamponade was the most common indication for RT (72/116 [62.1%]), although operative findings demonstrated exsanguinating haemorrhage in 82 patients (70.7%). Overall, 50 patients (43.1%) achieved return of spontaneous circulation and eight (6.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Survival was strongly associated with pathophysiological cause, duration of arrest, and physiological state at the time of intervention, with substantially better outcomes observed in patients with cardiac tamponade than exsanguination. Patients undergoing emergency department RT demonstrated shorter arrest durations, more favourable physiology, and higher survival than those undergoing prehospital RT. There were no survivors beyond 10 minutes of traumatic cardiac arrest. CONCLUSION: In this prospective national evaluation of RT practice, outcomes were strongly associated with the pathophysiological cause and duration of arrest, and the residual physiology present at the time of intervention. The most favourable outcomes were observed in patients with cardiac tamponade and those undergoing RT before irreversible physiological deterioration.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, and an increasing proportion of cases occur in lifetime nonsmokers, particularly East Asian women. Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in outdoor air pollution is classified as a Group 1 carcinogen and increasingly seen as an important modifiable exposure associated with lung cancer in nonsmokers. This narrative review summarizes epidemiologic and toxicological evidence linking environmental and microenvironmental PM2.5 exposures to lung cancer in nonsmokers, defined as individuals who have smoked fewer than 100 cigarettes in their lifetime. Global cohort and meta-analytic data, including dose-response findings and studies from Asian populations, are reviewed. Biological pathways linking PM2.5 to lung carcinogenesis are then examined, including oxidative stress, pulmonary inflammation, and particle-triggered cytokine and growth-factor signaling. Particular emphasis is placed on macrophage-derived interleukin-1β (IL-1β) signaling, which promotes epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. High-exposure microenvironments such as religious incense burning, residential cooking and solid-fuel use, urban transit systems (subway, bus, motorbike, and professional driving), and selected occupational settings (career and wildland firefighters, construction trades, informal e-waste recycling) are identified. These settings might contribute significantly to daily PM2.5 exposure in some individuals. Finally, future research priorities, including incorporation of cumulative PM2.5 exposure into lung cancer risk prediction models and development of cost-effective strategies for lung cancer screening in nonsmokers with high PM2.5 exposure, are presented.

METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised controlled trial, 914 adults were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either esketamine or normal saline. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Rapid and precise pathogen identification is crucial for managing lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs). While metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) and targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) are emerging as valuable diagnostic tools, large-scale studies directly evaluating their real-world impact on antimicrobial stewardship remain scarce. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study encompassing 941 patients with suspected LRTIs who underwent bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) sequencing. Patients were evaluated in either an mNGS cohort (n = 479; DNA-only sequencing) or a tNGS cohort (n = 462; DNA and RNA sequencing). Diagnostic performance, pathogen spectrum, and clinical utility were compared against a composite final clinical diagnosis, which served as the reference standard. RESULTS: Both sequencing platforms demonstrated diagnostic efficacy superior to traditional laboratory tests. In the tNGS cohort, polymicrobial infections were highly prevalent (93.5%). Furthermore, tNGS demonstrated high sensitivity for fastidious pathogens, identifying 54 cases of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (a cohort in which routine smears missed 77.8% of cases) and effectively detecting Pneumocystis jirovecii. The overall diagnostic sensitivity was 90.6% (95% CI: 87.5-93.1%) for mNGS and 73.4% (95% CI:69.2%-77.3%) for tNGS. Guided by tNGS results, clinicians escalated antimicrobial therapy in 22.6% of positive cases. The clinical improvement rate following this targeted escalation was 66.2%, comparable to the 66.7% improvement rate observed in patients receiving appropriate initial empirical therapy (P = 0.946). CONCLUSION: Both tNGS and mNGS offer substantial diagnostic value for LRTIs, with tNGS showing particular utility in identifying fastidious and low-titer pathogens. Sequencing-guided diagnostics frequently informed antimicrobial adjustments and were associated with favorable clinical progress; however, future prospective paired-testing studies are required to isolate the direct impact of sequencing on patient survival outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) is increasingly recognized in non-neutropenic patients, but validated bedside risk stratification tools remain scarce. We developed a machine learning model to predict IPA and tested whether corticosteroid effect depends on bacterial co-pathogen. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolled 837 non-neutropenic adults hospitalized with pulmonary infections across three tertiary hospitals in China between December 2020 and December 2025. The discovery cohort was split into training and internal validation sets. Four classifiers were compared, with Random Forest selected for optimal performance. The final model was externally validated in an independent cohort. Feature importance was assessed using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis. Corticosteroid-bacteria interactions were examined using subgroup analyses and propensity score matching, with the synergy index S calculated to quantify biological interaction. A simplified bedside score was derived from the top-ranking predictors. RESULTS: The Random Forest model achieved external validation AUC of 0.865. Six predictors consistently dominated across all assessments: Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation, hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 <200 mmHg), diabetes mellitus, organ failure (Sequential Organ Failure Assessment, SOFA >5), lymphopenia (lymphocyte count <0.8×109/L), and ICU (intensive care unit) admission. Corticosteroid exposure did not rank among the top six predictors. However, its association with IPA diverged sharply by bacterial context: OR below 1 with P. aeruginosa (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.214-1.283) but OR above 1 with other Gram-negative bacilli (OR 2.17, 95% CI 0.722-6.535); P for interaction = 0.131; a directional pattern that persisted after propensity matching. The six-variable score derived from these predictors showed AUCs of 0.869 (training), 0.774 (internal validation), and 0.719 (external validation). CONCLUSIONS: IPA risk in non-neutropenic ICU patients is shaped more by bacterial co-pathogen context than by corticosteroid exposure alone. The divergent corticosteroid effects across bacterial species challenge the conventional assumption of a uniform steroid-associated risk. The externally validated six-variable score offers a practical, software-free tool to support pathogen-informed, individualized risk stratification and clinical decision-making in the ICU.

papers.abstract_en: The aberrant inflammation that characterizes severe COVID-19 is incompletely understood. Given the persistence of SARS-Cov-2 RNA and nucleocapsid protein (N) and the presence of anti-N antibody during the course of severe infection, we investigated the role of RNA-containing immune complexes (ICs) in driving inflammation. We found that ICs consisting of SARS-CoV-2 RNA, N, and anti-N IgG1 are internalized by primary human monocytes and stimulate inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in a manner dependent on Fcγ receptors and partially dependent on toll-like receptor-8. In addition, the inflammatory response induced in monocytes by RNA-containing ICs caused endothelial dysfunction in vascularized micro-organs. Using nasopharyngeal samples from SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals, SARS-CoV-2 RNA and N were captured by anti-N monoclonal antibody in the absence of lysing reagents, indicating that SARS-CoV-2 RNA and N complexes are present outside of virions and cells. Finally, we found that during an early wave of COVID-19, higher anti-N IgG:IgM ratios were associated with more severe clinical outcomes, consistent with a role for inflammatory, IgG-mediated phagocytic clearance of nucleic acid-containing ICs in SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis, perhaps mitigated by non-inflammatory, IgM-mediated clearance. We conclude that RNA-containing ICs may play a role in the pathogenesis of severe COVID-19. Since all pathogenic viruses encode nucleic acid-binding proteins, such as N, and these proteins often elicit an antibody response, inflammatory clearance of nucleic acid-containing ICs may also contribute to disease severity in other viral infections.

papers.abstract_en: The frequency of lithium-ion battery (LIB) fires is increasing globally, creating new challenges for firefighters and growing public safety concerns from smoke and intense heat. However, the health effects from exposure to LIB fires are not well understood. We collected soot and smoke particulate matter (PM) from LIB thermal runaway events (10 and 2 fire tests for soot and PM samples, respectively), filtered them to remove non-inhalable particles (>10 μm), analyzed for chemical composition and assessed for lung toxicity and pulmonary function in mice at 4 h and 24 h post exposure to 100 μg of the sample. Chemical and biological results were analyzed using a computational approach to identify hazardous chemical components that were potentially responsible for toxicity outcomes. Computational findings were further compared to those produced by other sources of air pollution. The soot sample contained more carbon species than the smoke PM sample (37% vs. 18%), whereas anions were higher in the PM sample (12% vs. 6%), and concentrations of inorganic elements were similar (23% vs. 28%). Fluoride particulate was found to account for up to 5% of the mass of each sample. Only soot significantly increased ventilatory timing and peak expiratory flow in mice and decreased relaxation time, while both samples caused significant increases in inflammatory responses. Soot and PM exhibited similar lung inflammatory outcomes relative to those caused by previously reported combustion-related air pollution sources. Computational analysis indicated that fluoride, Al, Fe, Ni, and Li from both samples were significantly associated with the lung toxicity responses (p < 0.05). The findings indicate that LIB fire soot and PM that contain hazardous metals and fluoride elicit pulmonary toxicity responses comparable to other sources of air pollution, increasing the need for awareness of potential strategies to mitigate public health impacts.

papers.abstract_en: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects an estimated 936 million adults worldwide, yet how environmental exposures relate to sleep architecture and nocturnal oxygenation remains unclear. Interaction and mixture analyses further indicated meteorological modification and more consistent mixture relationships with altered sleep architecture than with categorical OSA severity. papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Immune cells express vitamin D receptors (VDR) and the CYP27B1 enzyme needed to produce the VDR ligand, 1,25(OH)2D; suggesting that perhaps the vitamin D response is regulated locally at the site of infection. Here, we examined the role of immune cell-derived 1,25(OH)2D in host resistance to influenza infection. METHODS: Mice were infected with mouse-adapted H1N1 influenza A virus, to determine the role of CYP27B1 on host resistance to influenza infection. RESULTS: Whole body Cyp27b1 KO mice developed severe influenza A virus disease, including infection induced mortality, compared to WT littermates. Oral treatments of the Cyp27b1 KO mice with 1,25(OH)2D failed to completely protect the Cyp27b1 KO mice from influenza A virus disease. Mice without renal 1,25(OH)2D had similar influenza disease as WT littermates. Influenza infection of T cell-specific Cyp27b1 KO resulted in increased respiratory distress and lethargy compared to WT littermates. WT and DIKO mice had more CD8+ T cells expressing higher amounts of granzyme B+ (GrzB) and disruptions in PD-1 than either whole-body Cyp27b1 KO or T-Cyp27b1 KO mice. DISCUSSION: The work suggests that renal 1,25(OH)2D is not required for host resistance to this influenza A virus infection. The work further demonstrates that immune cells and in particular T cells may produce 1,25(OH)2D to locally support CD8+ T cell responses to influenza A virus infection. Defining the mechanisms that regulate local 1,25(OH)2D production in T cells or other immune cell types is needed.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Sex-related differences in coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity suggest an important role for sex steroids in regulating immune and endothelial responses to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). METHODS: Receptor expression, inflammatory signaling, and monocyte transendothelial migration were assessed by RT-PCR, immunoblotting, and Boyden chamber assay, respectively. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in esophageal cancer, yet reliable biomarkers remain lacking. Tissue PD-L1 testing is limited by intratumoral heterogeneity and invasiveness, whereas circulating tumor cells (CTCs) offer a non-invasive alternative. This study evaluated CTC PD-L1 expression as a predictive and prognostic biomarker in patients with advanced esophageal cancer receiving chemo-immunotherapy. METHODS: A total of 93 patients with stage III-IV esophageal cancer were enrolled. The primary biomarker analysis was restricted to 59 patients who received chemo-immunotherapy, while 34 patients treated with chemotherapy alone were analyzed separately. Baseline CTCs were isolated and PD-L1 expression assessed, alongside tissue PD-L1 (tPD-L1) by immunohistochemistry. Associations with objective response rate (ORR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using ROC curves and univariate and multivariable Cox regression. RESULTS: CTC positivity correlated significantly with advanced stage, metastasis (p = 0.0411), and larger tumor size (p = 0.0454). In the chemo-immunotherapy cohort, CTC PD-L1 positivity was associated with a higher ORR (75.0% vs. 29.6%, p < 0.001) and showed moderate predictive ability (AUC = 0.7049, p = 0.0037). CTC PD-L1 positivity was significantly associated with OS (HR = 0.254, p = 0.002), but not significantly with PFS in univariate analysis (HR = 0.546, p = 0.042; Kaplan-Meier p = 0.061). Conversely, tPD-L1 status was not significantly associated with PFS or OS (both p > 0.05). In multivariable analysis adjusting for age, sex, histological subtype, stage, metastasis, and treatment modality, CTC PD-L1 remained an independent prognostic factor for PFS (HR = 0.488, p = 0.039) and OS (HR = 0.244, p = 0.002). CONCLUSIONS: Baseline CTC PD-L1 expression was associated with favorable response and OS in patients receiving chemo-immunotherapy, and may complement tissue testing. These exploratory findings require prospective validation in larger cohorts before clinical use.

papers.abstract_en: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) undergo functional reprogramming that critically regulates lung inflammation. Although mitophagy is essential for mitochondrial quality control, its role in macrophage functional reprogramming during acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains unclear. Here, we identify the nuclear receptor Nr1h4 (FXR) as a transcriptional regulator of mitophagy in AMs. FXR activation transcriptionally upregulates serine palmitoyltransferase long chain base subunit 2 (Sptlc2), thereby enhancing mitophagy and promoting an anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotype under inflammatory conditions. Conversely, FXR deficiency impairs mitophagy, exacerbates pulmonary inflammation, and aggravates lung injury in vivo. These findings establish the FXR/Sptlc2 axis as a regulator of mitochondrial quality control and macrophage functional reprogramming and identify it as a potential therapeutic target in ARDS.

papers.abstract_en: The phosphoinositide-dependent kinase-1 (PDK1)-Akt signaling pathway plays a central role in regulating diverse cellular processes, including cell growth, survival, and metabolism. Dysregulation of this pathway is frequently observed in malignancies and is associated with tumor progression and resistance to therapy. Despite the recognized therapeutic potential of PDK1, potent and selective inhibitors remain limited. In this study, we developed and characterized a novel PDK1 inhibitor, SD-2102, and evaluated its anticancer effects in vitro and in vivo. A novel small-molecule compound, SD-2102, was synthesized and screened for PDK1 inhibitory activity. Binding affinity and interaction sites were examined using biochemical assays to identify the targeted domain. Functional assays, including cell proliferation, cell cycle analysis, and apoptosis detection, were performed in cancer cell lines. The in vivo efficacy of SD-2102 was assessed using a xenograft model. SD-2102 was predicted to interact with the pleckstrin homology domain of PDK1 and reduced PDK1 plasma membrane translocation. This inhibition led to decreased phosphorylation and activation of Akt. In vitro, SD-2102 suppressed cancer cell proliferation by inducing G1 phase arrest and promoting apoptosis. Importantly, SD-2102 induced minimal apoptosis in BEAS-2B non-tumorigenic human bronchial epithelial cells, supporting a preferential apoptotic effect toward lung cancer cells. In vivo, treatment with SD-2102 significantly reduced tumor growth in the xenograft model, consistent with the cellular findings. Together, these findings suggest that SD-2102 suppresses PDK1/Akt signaling while exhibiting preferential anticancer activity in lung cancer cells, supporting its further development as an anticancer agent.

papers.abstract_en: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is one of the most aggressive and rapidly progressing forms of lung cancer, characterized by its high proliferative rate and strong tendency to metastasize. Although SCLC initially responds well to platinum-based chemotherapy, resistance typically develops quickly, leaving few effective options and resulting in poor overall survival. Immunotherapies, including PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors have been introduced in clinical settings and other drugs, such as antibody-drug conjugates, are being actively studied, but their efficacy has so far been limited. Despite a shared genetic foundation, most notably the near-universal loss of tumor suppressor genes TP53 and RB1, alongside frequent over-activation of the MYC family of oncogenes (MYC, MYCN, MYCL), SCLC exhibits remarkable diversity at the molecular level. Historically, classification of SCLC was based on the presence or absence of neuroendocrine features. However, recent advances have shifted the paradigm toward a transcription factor-driven framework that defines molecular subtypes. One of the key areas of current investigation is understanding the multifaceted role of oncogenic activation of MYC family members in SCLC biology. Given its prominent involvement in driving certain subtypes of the disease, it represents a critical axis of vulnerability that may be exploited for therapeutic use. By dissecting how MYC oncogenic activity varies across molecular subtypes, this review aims to highlight novel opportunities for targeted interventions that could improve clinical outcomes for specific patient populations. This review explores the underlying mechanisms that drive SCLC initiation and progression, focusing on tumor heterogeneity, immune landscape, and especially the role of oncogenic MYC in promoting metastasis and therapeutic resistance. We further explore how recent insights into these processes are shaping emerging treatment strategies, with an emphasis on targeting molecular vulnerabilities within distinct MYC-driven subtypes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dysregulated epithelial alarmin release is a key driver of chronic airway inflammation in asthma. Interleukin-33 (IL-33), released from activated airway epithelial cells, amplifies type 2 immune responses, yet the upstream mechanisms that link epithelial stress to IL-33 secretion remain incompletely defined. We investigated whether circGDI2 contributed to epithelial IL-33 release and allergic airway inflammation. METHODS: circGDI2 expression was examined in IL-13-stimulated BEAS-2B cells. Its functional role was evaluated in a house dust mite (HDM)-induced murine asthma model using adeno-associated virus-mediated circGDI2 knockdown, miR-103a-3p agomir, and NLRP3 siRNA. Molecular interactions were assessed by dual-luciferase reporter assays, RNA pull-down, and fluorescence in situ hybridization. NLRP3 inflammasome activation was monitored by cleaved caspase-1 p20, mature IL-1β, and IL-18 secretion, along with LDH release. RESULTS: circGDI2 was upregulated in IL-13-stimulated BEAS-2B cells. circGDI2 silencing alleviated airway inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and remodeling, and reduced type 2 immune responses in HDM-exposed mice. Mechanistically, circGDI2 sponged miR-103a-3p to derepress NLRP3 and promoted epithelial IL-33 release, accompanied by increased cleaved caspase-1 p20 and mature IL-1β and IL-18 secretion together with only a limited and NLRP3-dependent increase in LDH release. Consistent with this, miR-103a-3p restoration, NLRP3 knockdown, or MCC950 treatment each attenuated airway inflammation and IL-33 release, confirming the circGDI2/miR-103a-3p/NLRP3 axis. CONCLUSIONS: circGDI2 promotes allergic airway inflammation by enhancing epithelial IL-33 release through the miR-103a-3p/NLRP3 pathway. These findings support circGDI2 as an upstream regulator of inflammatory responses in experimental asthma.

papers.abstract_en: Acute lung injury (ALI) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are life-threatening conditions with high mortality. Excessive neutrophil activation and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-related responses, together with pulmonary endothelial barrier impairment, are critical pathological features. Heat shock protein A12B (HSPA12B) has endothelial-protective and anti-inflammatory functions, but its relationship with the PKC-PAD4 pathway and neutrophil-associated lung injury remains unclear. In this study, we combined bioinformatics analysis with an LPS-induced ALI mouse model to examine whether HSPA12B expression is associated with PKC-PAD4 pathway activation and neutrophil-related lung injury. HSPA12B overexpression was associated with reduced pathological lung damage, lower levels of inflammatory cytokines and oxidative stress markers, as well as decreased lung-tissue levels of PKC, PAD4 and neutrophil-associated markers (CitH3, MPO, NE). Conversely, HSPA12B knockdown was accompanied by elevated protein levels of PKC, aggravated lung injury, and further upregulation of these markers; transcriptomic analysis of lungs from HSPA12B-knockdown mice revealed enrichment of the neutrophil extracellular trap formation pathway. These findings indicate that HSPA12B is functionally linked to the PKC-PAD4 cascade and neutrophil-mediated lung injury in LPS-induced ALI. Of note, the PKC-PAD4 link is proposed rather than directly demonstrated, and that isoform-specific and activity-level evidence is still lacking. This study identifies HSPA12B as a potential upstream regulatory node for further mechanistic investigation, providing a basis for future HSPA12B-targeted studies in ALI/ARDS.

papers.abstract_en: Right ventricular (RV) failure is the major cause of mortality in pulmonary hypertension (PH). Adaptive angiogenesis and RV endothelial cell (RVEC) function are major modifiers of RV adaptation in PH, but the underlying mechanisms and their regulators remain incompletely understood. RV adaptation in PH is sexually dimorphic, and 17β-estradiol (E2) exerts protective effects on RV cardiomyocytes. Whether E2 modifies angiogenesis and RVEC function in RV failure remains unknown. We hypothesized that E2 and estrogen receptor α (ERα) promote RV angiogenesis and RVEC homeostasis in PH and aimed to identify underlying mechanisms. We assessed E2's angiogenic effects using cultured human cardiac microvascular endothelial cells (hCMVECs), RVECs from PH patients with RV failure, and RVECs from sugen/hypoxia (SuHx) and monocrotaline rat models. In vivo, we evaluated RV capillary density in PH rats treated with E2 or ERα-selective agonist. Apelin signaling was evaluated via apelin receptor (APLNR) blockade and knockdown studies. E2 preserved angiogenesis in male hCMVECs and RV capillary density in male and female SuHx-PH rats. E2 reversed angiogenic alterations in RVECs from SuHx-PH rats via APLNR signaling. In RVECs from RV failure patients, E2 stimulated vascular network formation. In rat and human PH-RVECs, ERα was necessary and sufficient to mediate E2-induced angiogenesis. Activation of ERα with ERα-specific agonist restored RV capillary density in vivo. ERα-mediated angiogenesis required apelin signaling. These data indicate that E2 promotes RV angiogenesis via ERα and apelin signaling and identify a novel ERα-apelin axis in RVECs as a potential therapeutic target to restore RV vascular integrity in PH.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is frequent after traumatic brain injury (TBI), but its biological meaning and outcome impact remain incompletely defined. Traditional models emphasise mechanical ventilation, aspiration, colonisation, endotracheal tube biofilm, and hospital pathogens. These mechanisms remain essential, but they do not fully explain the early clustering, heterogeneous susceptibility, changing bacteriology, and variable mortality effect observed after TBI. MAIN TEXT: Severe brain injury creates an early vulnerable host state through impaired consciousness and airway protection, neuroimmune dysregulation, autonomic and endocrine activation, altered pulmonary immune surveillance, and, in many patients, extracranial trauma, shock, transfusion, or thoracic injury. These processes interact with ventilation, antibiotic pressure, and rapid respiratory microbiome disruption. Early VAP may reflect abrupt loss of control after injury and intubation, whereas late VAP may reflect persistent or secondary failure driven by biofilm maturation, antibiotic selection, multidrug-resistant pathogens, and intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired immune dysfunction. Clinically, VAP consistently prolongs ventilation, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and resource use, while its independent effect on mortality is phenotype- and context-dependent. CONCLUSIONS: This model proposes a timing-sensitive ecological framework in which established mechanisms may converge early and with particular clinical intensity after severe TBI, creating a vulnerable host-microbe state that may lower the threshold for clinically apparent infection. Future studies should distinguish isolated TBI from polytrauma, compare TBI with other acute brain injuries and non-neurological ventilated populations, and incorporate dynamic immune, microbial, and trajectory-based outcomes. HIGHLIGHTS: VAP after TBI should be viewed as a timing-sensitive interaction between ventilator exposure and early host vulnerability, not as a distinct disease entity or as a pneumonia pathway unique to traumatic brain injury. The TBI-focused contribution lies in the early convergence of otherwise non-unique mechanisms: impaired airway control, aspiration risk, neuroimmune-endocrine activation, treatment exposure, dysbiosis, and extracranial injury burden, rather than in any single TBI-specific mechanism. Isolated TBI and TBI with polytrauma are biologically different phenotypes and should be separated in future studies. Early and late VAP may represent different phases of loss of pulmonary host-microbe containment; this distinction is probabilistic rather than TBI-specific in itself and requires validation in TBI-stratified cohorts. Mortality remains clinically relevant but context-dependent; VAP more consistently modifies recovery trajectory, ventilator dependence, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and possibly neurological recovery.

papers.abstract_en: Although SerpinE3, an extracellular serine protease inhibitor, has been documented in several studies, its biological function remains largely undefined. In a screen for interactors of TMPRSS11E-a protease known to exacerbate inflammation and lung injury during infection-we identified a novel interaction with SerpinE3. Initially, we assessed the inhibitory effect of SerpinE3 on TMPRSS11E activity using synthetic fluorescent substrates PAR1 and PAR2 peptides. We further characterized SerpinE3 expression patterns in mouse cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) models of inflammation and in patients with pneumonia. Subsequently, the anti-inflammatory effects of SerpinE3 were investigated in both in vitro and in vivo inflammatory models. Finally, we examined the regulatory mechanisms governing SerpinE3 expression via promoter activity assays and electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSA). Our results demonstrate that SerpinE3 directly inhibits TMPRSS11E activity. SerpinE3 expression was significantly upregulated in alveolar and liver macrophages under inflammatory conditions. Administration of recombinant SerpinE3 protein markedly alleviated inflammation and acute lung injury in the mouse CLP model. Conversely, SerpinE3 knockout mice exhibited aggravated lung injury, a phenotype that was rescued by recombinant protein administration. Notably, aged SerpinE3 knockout mice displayed a spontaneous accumulation of inflammatory cells in the lungs. Mechanistically, we identified a functional NF-κB response element within the proximal promoter of SerpinE3. In conclusion, we identify SerpinE3 as an infection-inducible, macrophage-derived regulator that attenuates inflammatory lung injury, likely through the inhibition of TMPRSS11E. This study elucidates a critical anti-inflammatory role for SerpinE3 and paves the way for developing SerpinE3-based therapies for inflammatory acute lung injury.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To access whether a structured, facility-level quality improvement (QI) approach using an adapted tuberculosis (TB) Building and Strengthening Infection Control Strategies (TB BASICS) methodology could improve TB infection prevention and control (IPC) practices in outpatient TB clinics in Vietnam. METHODS: From October 2022 to September 2023, 11 health care facilities in Ho Chi Minh City implemented QI interventions with local experts' mentorship. A context- adapted assessment evaluated 103 indicators across four IPC domains. Baseline and final assessments were conducted before and after six months of QI implementation, with progress measured by percent change in average scores. RESULTS: All IPC domains improved across all facilities. Environmental controls showed the largest improvement (89.6%), followed by respiratory protection (62.4%), IPC core components (57.7%), and administrative controls (31.0%). Low-cost ventilation measures contributed to ≥12 air changes per hour in 20 of 34 (58.8%) targeted areas. Improvements were also observed in IPC guidelines, compliance monitoring, respiratory protection policies, fit testing; although gaps in patient fast-tracking, separation practices, and respirator availability remained. CONCLUSIONS: A structured, mentor- supported, tailored QI initiative was associated with improved TB IPC practices and provides a scalable framework for strengthening TB IPC in health care settings vulnerable to TB and other airborne threats.

papers.abstract_en: In this study, we aimed to investigate whether 6-hydroxyrubiadin (6-HR), a compound derived from the root of Rubia akane Nakai, exerts a regulatory effect on the gene expression of MUC5AC mucin under conditions mimicking pulmonary inflammation in human airway epithelial cells. Confluent NCI-H292 cells were pretreated with 6-HR for 30 min, followed by stimulation with tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α for 24 h. MUC5AC mRNA expression and glycoprotein production were measured using reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), respectively. Further, we examined the effect of 6-HR on TNF-α-induced activation of the nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathways via immunoblot analysis. The results were as follows: (1) 6-HR significantly reduced both the production of MUC5AC glycoprotein and MUC5AC mRNA expression in NCI-H292 cells. (2) 6-HR inhibited TNF-α-induced NF-κB activation through a transforming growth factor-β-activated kinase 1 (TAK1)-dependent mechanism. (3) 6-HR also inhibited TAK1-dependent MAPK signaling pathways activated by TNF-α, resulting in the downregulation of MUC5AC mucin production in NCI-H292 cells. These findings suggest that 6-HR regulates the gene expression of MUC5AC mucin by directly acting on airway epithelial cells through modulation of the MAPK and NF-κB signaling pathways.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the acceptance of Tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) and the factors associated with treatment acceptance among individuals aged ≥60 years that screened positive for latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) in Huzhou city, Zhejiang Province of China, and to provide scientific evidence for TPT implementation in this population. METHODS: Older adults aged ≥60 years with LTBI were recruited through community-based health examinations and screening of close contacts of active tuberculosis patients. Univariate and multivariate Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with TPT acceptance. RESULTS: Of the 620 participants enrolled, 430 (69.35%) accepted TPT. Among the participants, 354 (57.09%) were male, 192 (30.96%) were aged over 70 years, 593 (95.65%) were married, 499 (80.48%) resided in rural areas, 577 (93.06%) had an education level of junior high school or below, 135 (21.77%) smoked daily or occasionally, and 152 (24.52%) consumed alcohol occasionally or at least twice weekly. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis revealed that participants with a household size of ≤3 persons (aOR: 1.88; 95% CI: 1.15-3.07), an annual household income of ≤150, 000 CNY (aOR: 2.24; 95% CI: 1.33-3.77), and a history of underlying diseases (aOR: 1.86; 95% CI: 1.16-2.99) were more likely to accept TPT. CONCLUSION: The TPT acceptance rate among older adults aged ≥60 years with LTBI in Huzhou was relatively high. Acceptance was independently associated with household structure, economic status, and health status. Smaller household size (≤3 persons), lower annual household income (≤150, 000 CNY), and the presence of underlying diseases were independently associated with TPT acceptance in this population. Targeted intervention strategies should be developed for older adults from larger households, those with better economic conditions, and those without underlying diseases to improve overall TPT coverage.

papers.abstract_en: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global public health challenge, with treatment complicated by drug resistance, adverse effects, and suboptimal host immune responses. Whilst conventional anti-TB drugs are effective bactericidally, their immunomodulatory effects may, in certain contexts, contribute to immune imbalance and affect treatment outcomes. Host-directed therapy (HDT), which aims to modulate the host immune response to enhance pathogen control and limit immunopathology, has emerged as a promising adjunctive strategy. This narrative review critically evaluates the current evidence for HDT in TB, focusing on immunosenescence, trained immunity, cytokine and lipid mediator networks, immunometabolic reprogramming, neuroendocrine regulation, and repurposed drugs including metformin and statins. Importantly, we distinguish between evidence derived directly from TB models (in vitro, animal, and clinical studies) and evidence extrapolated from other diseases, highlighting knowledge gaps and areas requiring further investigation. We propose that future progress depends on evidence-based stratification of HDT candidates, rigorous clinical trial design, and a personalised approach that accounts for patient comorbidities and immune status. This review aims to provide a balanced framework for advancing HDT from bench to bedside in TB therapy.
